quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #8
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down or stop.
Stop if necessary.
You must come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: An octagonal sign always means stop. You must come to a complete stop at the marked stop line. Stop before the crosswalk if there is no stop line. Stop before the intersection if there is no crosswalk. Only proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign warn drivers about?

options.text: Upcoming intersections.
Road construction.
Road curves ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road curves ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to conditions just ahead. This sign warns drivers about an upcoming curve to the right.

questions.question: What does this yellow warning sign mean?

options.text: You are approaching a school or school crosswalk.
Slow down, drive with caution, and watch for children.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: This sign is placed on roads near schools. It warns you to slow down, drive with caution, and watch for children.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on water instead of the road surface. How can you prevent hydroplaning in rain?

options.text: Put on your cruise control to maintain a constant speed.
Decrease your speed.
Move to the shoulder of the road as soon as it starts to rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Decrease your speed.
questions.explanation: In rainy weather, slow down to reduce hydroplaning risk. Driving too fast causes tires to ride on water and lose contact with the road. This makes it very hard to control your vehicle.

questions.question: If you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, you must:

options.text: Slow down because the lane ends ahead.
Be prepared for workers and equipment ahead.
Change lanes and maintain your current speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be prepared for workers and equipment ahead.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs warn you of workers, slow equipment, and closed lanes ahead. Reduce your speed and be ready to slow down or stop.

questions.question: When are collisions more likely to happen?

options.text: All vehicles are traveling at about the same speed.
One lane of traffic is traveling faster than the other lanes.
One vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: One vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: Collisions happen more often when one driver travels faster or slower than other vehicles. Driving faster increases your collision risk. Driving slower also increases risk of rear-end collisions or causes other drivers to swerve to avoid you.

questions.question: Where should drivers be especially alert to children?

options.text: School zones and playgrounds
Residential neighborhoods
All of the above locations

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above locations
questions.explanation: Use extreme caution wherever children are playing or gathering. This includes schools, playgrounds, and neighborhoods where children may play in the streets.

questions.question: When merging onto the freeway, you should drive:

options.text: At or near the speed of the freeway traffic.
At the legal speed limit.
More slowly than the freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of the freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Enter the freeway at or near the speed of traffic. Do not exceed the legal speed limit when doing so.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line between two lanes of traffic mean?

options.text: Both lanes of traffic are going in the same direction.
Passing is permitted when it's safe.
Passing is not permitted.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is permitted when it's safe.
questions.explanation: Dashed yellow lines separate single lanes moving in opposite directions. Passing is allowed when there is no oncoming traffic in the passing lane.

questions.question: When driving on slippery surfaces like snow or ice, what should you do?

options.text: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
Maintain traction by following other vehicles closely.
Pump your brakes to keep them from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
questions.explanation: Shift to low gear before going down steep hills to prevent skidding on slippery surfaces. Follow farther behind other vehicles than normal. Avoid quick stops. Pump your brakes to slow or stop, unless you have antilock brakes.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines in the center of the road mean for passing?

options.text: You can pass from either direction.
You can pass only from your direction.
You cannot pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double yellow lines mean no one can cross the center line to pass, no matter which direction they are traveling.

questions.question: What type of sign is this?

options.text: Service sign.
Regulatory sign.
Warning sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about dangers ahead, such as a sharp turn, steep hill, or hazard. You need to be ready to slow down or change how you drive.

questions.question: When making a left turn, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Signal to other drivers.
Cut the corner.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cut the corner.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal and slow down at least 100 feet before turning left. Do not cut the corner short. This can hit other vehicles.

questions.question: What should you do when you reach a traffic light that is not working?

options.text: Come to a full stop and yield before entering the intersection.
You do not need to stop if the intersection looks clear.
Drive quickly through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop and yield before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: Treat a broken traffic light like a four-way stop. Always stop completely and look both ways before entering.

questions.question: Which statement about drugs and driving is true?

options.text: Prescription drugs are safe if you don't feel drowsy.
Over-the-counter drugs can also hurt your driving.
Only illegal drugs can hurt your driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over-the-counter drugs can also hurt your driving.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter drugs can make it unsafe to drive. This includes drugs for colds, allergies, and anxiety. It is illegal to drive while any drug impairs your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: If your wheels go off the road edge, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until it is safe, then slowly return to the road.
Turn back onto the road right away.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until it is safe, then slowly return to the road.
questions.explanation: Do not turn back onto the road immediately. Instead, slow down and check traffic. Gradually turn back when it is safe.

questions.question: At what speed can water on the road cause your car to hydroplane?

options.text: 45 miles per hour.
35 miles per hour.
40 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: 35 miles per hour.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when there is water on the road. Most tires can handle water at speeds up to 35 mph. Above 35 mph, tires cannot move water away fast enough and may slide on top of the water.

questions.question: When should you not enter an intersection if you will block it when the light turns red?

options.text: Under any circumstances.
Unless you entered on a yellow light.
Unless you entered on a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under any circumstances.
questions.explanation: Even if the light is green, only enter the intersection if you can drive all the way across before it turns red. Blocking the intersection can result in a ticket.

questions.question: After a train passes at a railroad crossing, what should you do?

options.text: Wait for the signal lights to stop flashing.
Look for a second train.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Another train may be coming on another track. Do not go forward until all gates are up and all warning lights stop flashing.

questions.question: At night, an oncoming car has its high beams on and it is hard to see. Where should you look?

options.text: Look toward the left edge of your lane.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.
Look straight ahead in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at the headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of your lane and watch the other car from the corner of your eye.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spot when changing lanes?

options.text: Use the inside rearview mirror.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
Use your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Mirrors cannot show all blind spots. Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder to see these hidden areas.

questions.question: What should you do when merging onto an interstate highway?

options.text: Find a safe gap and merge into the traffic lane.
Merge across two lanes at once.
Always stop before entering the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe gap and merge into the traffic lane.
questions.explanation: Look for a gap large enough to enter traffic safely. Do not stop on the entrance ramp unless you cannot find a safe gap to merge into.

questions.question: Interstate driving requires drivers to:

options.text: Safely drive at higher speeds.
Stay alert at all times.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Safe interstate driving requires you to stay alert and be able to drive at high speeds.

questions.question: Why is night driving more dangerous than day driving?

options.text: You cannot see as far ahead.
The road is always more slippery at night.
Your reaction time is slower at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far ahead.
questions.explanation: Poor visibility and glare from oncoming headlights reduce how far you can see at night. Always use your headlights and drive carefully in the dark.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in a construction zone?

options.text: Slightly increase your speed.
Expect the unexpected.
Expect construction workers to yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expect the unexpected.
questions.explanation: Construction zones have unpredictable conditions. Drive with extra caution to protect yourself, other drivers, and construction workers.

questions.question: Who can drivers legally obey instructions from?

options.text: Security guards in parking lots.
Drivers whose vehicles are broken down.
Flaggers at construction sites.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flaggers at construction sites.
questions.explanation: Drivers must obey flaggers and their signals. They are there to keep everyone safe.

questions.question: Why should you signal continuously while turning?

options.text: It is illegal to turn off your signal before completing a turn.
It tells other drivers what you plan to do.
It is always unsafe to turn off a signal before completing a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: It tells other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Always signal when turning, changing lanes, slowing down, or stopping. This tells other drivers, motorcyclists, cyclists, and pedestrians what you intend to do.

questions.question: A police officer tells you to go through a red traffic light. What should you do?

options.text: Stop until the light turns green.
Go through the intersection without stopping.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go through the intersection without stopping.
questions.explanation: Police officers directing traffic override traffic signals and signs. Follow their instructions.

questions.question: When should your wheels NOT be pointed straight ahead?

options.text: When waiting to turn left at a traffic light.
When parked on a hill or slope.
When parked on a level roadway with no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When parked on a hill or slope.
questions.explanation: Keep wheels straight when waiting to turn left. If hit from behind, this prevents you from sliding into oncoming traffic. On hills, turn wheels toward the curb or downhill to prevent rolling if brakes fail.

questions.question: When must you use your low beam headlights?

options.text: On a lighted street.
On a freeway.
In fog.

questions.correctAnswerText: In fog.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off water and create glare, making it harder to see. Some vehicles have fog lights to use with low beams.
